Numerical criteria then produce explicit Hodge--Riemann classes, Lefschetz isomorphisms in bidegree $(1,1)$, and weighted Hodge-index inequalities.

papers.title: Stability of vector bundles and reduction mod $p$
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be a vector bundle on a normal complex projective variety. We prove that slope stability of $\mathop{Sym}^2E$ and Zariski density of the reductions of $E$ modulo $p$ that are not strongly geometrically stable imply that the bundle $E$ is projectively unitary flat. This generalizes Shepherd--Barron's result from rank $2$ to arbitrary rank. We also show that if $E$ has rank $\le 3$ we can replace stability of $\mathop{Sym}^2E$ by stability of $E$ but we cannot do so if $E$ has rank $4$. We also generalize these results to reflexive sheaves on some mildly singular normal complex projective varieties.

papers.title: Stable reduction and large Nielsen orbits on generalized Markoff surfaces
papers.abstract: We establish lower bounds on the orbit cardinalities of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ on the $\mathbb{F}_p$-points of the generalized Markoff surfaces given by $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz = τ+2$. We show that outside of the reductions of a certain exceptional finite set of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-points found by Dubrovin and Mazzocco, every orbit has cardinality $\ge p$. Together with a recent result of Nathaniel Kingsbury-Neuschotz, this establishes, for all but finitely many primes $p$, the classification conjectures of McCullough-Wanderley (2013), and gives a complete classification of the connected components of the Hurwitz stack of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of elliptic curves, only branched above the origin. This extends earlier work of Bourgain-Gamburd-Sarnak and the author in the Markoff case $τ= -2$. Our method studies certain noncongruence modular curves attached to a $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$-orbit. These modular curves parametrize elliptic curves with a $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-cover. We use this moduli interpretation to show that the noncongruence modular curves involved have bad reduction, as a cover of the $j$-line, at some place above $p$. This implies that the degree of the cover is $\ge p$, which translates into the desired bound on orbits. Key inputs include a result of Bouw-Wewers on bad reduction of three-point $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of the projective line, and the general stable reduction theory of Henrio, Obus, Raynaud, and Wewers.

papers.title: Stein degree over fields of characteristic zero
papers.abstract: We show that the Stein degree of horizontal divisors on generalised log Calabi-Yau fibrations or certain vertical divisors of Fano type fibrations over arbitrary fields of characteristic zero is bounded by constants that are independent on the ground field.

papers.title: Strongly regular graphs on 160, 232, 261 and 280 vertices from fusions of orbitals of PΓL(2,8) and 2^4:(S3×S3)
papers.abstract: We construct strongly regular graphs with parameters (160,54,18,18), (232,63,14,18), (261,64,14,16) and (280,63,14,14), and hence also their complements. All four parameter sets were marked "?" (existence unknown) in Brouwer's online table on 11 and 12 October 2026; they are the parameters of the hypothetical partial geometries pg(9,5,3), pg(7,8,2), pg(8,7,2) and pg(9,6,2). We give eight pairwise non-isomorphic graphs: three on 160 vertices, one on 232, two on 261 and two on 280. None of them is geometric. As far as we can determine, they are the first graphs known with these parameters. Five of the graphs have a short description over the projective line PG(1,8) and its quadratic extension PG(1,64). The vertices are pairs of points of PG(1,8) or conjugate pairs of points of PG(1,64) ∖ PG(1,8), each carrying a label in 𝔽_8*, together with a small orbit of points, pairs, or conjugate pairs. Adjacency is decided by cross ratios: for two labelled vertices on disjoint pairs, the quotient (or the product) of the two labels must equal the cross ratio of the two pairs or its inverse; for pairs sharing a point it must equal 1, and a labelled pair and a conjugate pair are adjacent when their cross ratio is a primitive cube root of unity. The "quotient" graphs on 232, 261 and 280 vertices have the automorphism group (SL(2,8) × C_7) ⋊ C_6 ≅ GL(2,8) ⋊ C_6 of order 21168; the two "product" graphs have C_2 × PΓL(2,8), of order 3024. One graph on 160 vertices lives on the 16 cells of a 4 × 4 grid and three copies of the 48 flags of its even transversals; its automorphism group is C_3 × 2^4:(S_3 × S_3), of order 1728. The other two graphs on 160 vertices have automorphism groups of orders 1728 and 576. The graphs were found by a computer search over fusions of orbitals of groups acting with two or three orbits, using the GAP library of tables of marks; the search reported five graphs, and enumerating all fusions of the same group actions gave three more. We do not classify the graphs with these parameters. The same constructions over PG(1,q) give, for q=4, the classical skew-lines graph of PG(3,2) and a second known srg(35,16,6,8), and no strongly regular graph for q=16 or q=32 under the groups searched (complete solver verdicts): within this model the graphs for q=8 appear to be sporadic. Strong regularity of every graph is checked by an exact, standalone, standard-library Python program, the constructions are re-implemented from the text of this paper, and all computer results were reproduced by an independent audit with separately written code and checked again by a referee with its own code. Also deposited on Zenodo with the full data archive (the citable record): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23313399

papers.title: Tate cohomology of unipotent cuspidal representations of finite groups of Lie type
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and $k$ be an algebraic closure of the finite field with $p$ elements. Let $G$ be a connected reductive algebraic group over $k$, and let $F:G\rightarrow G$ be a Frobenius morphism, defining an $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational structure on $G$, where $q$ is a power of $p$. Let $\ell$ be a prime different from $p$ and $\ell\ne 2$. Let $Π$ be an $\ell$-adic cuspidal unipotent representation of $G^{F^\ell}$ such that $Π\simeq Π^σ$, where $σ$ is a generator the Galois group ${\rm Gal}(\mathbb{F}_{q^\ell}/\mathbb{F}_q)$. In this paper, we prove the irreducibility of the zeroth Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^0(σ,\mathcal{L})$ and vanishing of the first Tate cohomology group $\widehat{\rm H}^1(σ,\mathcal{L})$ for any $G^{F^\ell}\rtimes{\rm Gal}(\mathbb{F}_{q^\ell}/\mathbb{F}_q)$-stable lattice $\mathcal{L}$ in $Π$, using the multiplicity-one property of a progenerator constructed via the generalized Gelfand-Graev representations and Harish-Chandra induction.

papers.title: The a-number of the Serre-type maximal curves of Abdón-Bezerra-Quoos
papers.abstract: For every prime power $q$, we determine the $a$-number of the Serre-type maximal curves $X(q,n)$: $y^{q^2}-y=x^{(q^n+1)/(q+1)}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^{2n}}$, $n\ge 3$ odd, introduced by Abdón, Bezerra and Quoos as a generalization of Serre's curve $y^4+y=x^3$ over $\mathbb{F}_{64}$. The Weierstrass semigroup at the unique point at infinity gives an explicit basis of holomorphic differentials, on which the Cartier operator acts by monomials; this reduces the $a$-number to a lattice-point count, which we evaluate in closed form.

papers.title: The canonical class and Chern character operators on Hilbert schemes of points
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex surface. We obtain explicit formulas for the Chern character operators on the Hilbert schemes of points $X^{[n]}$ in terms of Nakajima operators, determining in particular the coefficients of the terms involving the canonical class $K_X$ and its square. Consequently, the cohomology ring structure of the Hilbert scheme is determined. As an application, we give an alternative proof of the action of the affine Yangian $Y_{t_1,t_2}(\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_1)$ on the cohomological Fock space $\mathbb{H}_X = \bigoplus_{n\geq 0} H^*(X^{[n]},\mathbb{Q})$.

papers.title: The Cartan determinant conjecture for representation-finite algebras over perfect fields
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field and let $A$ be a finite-dimensional representation-finite $k$-algebra. We prove that finite global dimension implies that the integral Cartan determinant of $A$ is one, extending Enomoto's result from algebraically closed fields to perfect fields.

papers.title: The Chaise Longue Theorem: Conjecture 1.2 of Degtyarev–Shimada for the Fermat varieties of every degree in every even dimension, and the integral Hodge conjecture for those whose degree is prime, equal to 4, or prime to (n+1)!
papers.abstract: Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^{n+1}$ be the complex Fermat variety of degree $m \ge 3$ and even dimension $n = 2k$, and let $L(X) \subseteq H_n(X; \mathbb{Z})$ be the subgroup generated by the classes of its standard $k$-dimensional linear subspaces. Degtyarev and Shimada conjectured that $H_n(X; \mathbb{Z})/L(X)$ is torsion free [DS, Conjecture 1.2]. We prove this conjecture for every degree $m \ge 3$ in every even dimension, modulo two topological results used by [DS]: Pham's theorem on the homology of the affine Fermat variety, and their intersection numbers. Its algebraic form — the quotient $\mathbb{Z}[G]/(\psi_J)$ of the group ring of [DS] is free abelian of rank $m^{2k+1} - Q_k(m)$ — is proved with no topology, and it has been verified for every degree by a complete proof in the proof assistant Lean 4 with the Mathlib library, with no gap and no axiom beyond the three standard ones. The proof reduces the conjecture, prime by prime, to dimension counts in truncated polynomial rings, proved by peeling off one variable at a time. Consequences: the integral Hodge conjecture for $X$ whenever $m$ is prime, or $m = 4$, or $m$ is prime to $(n+1)!$, with the integral Hodge classes of middle degree generated by the standard linear subspaces — in particular for the Fermat quartic of every even dimension; and the primitivity of the sublattices spanned by the linear subspaces that [DS] exhibit on the partial Fermat varieties, which [DS] proved conditionally on the conjecture. This work has not been refereed by a human expert.

papers.title: The fifteenth cohomology group of moduli spaces of stable curves
papers.abstract: The new framework of semi-tautological extensions has allowed for explicit understanding of low-degree odd cohomology groups of moduli spaces of stable curves. Let $S^*_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) \subset H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ denote the semi-tautological extension generated by $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$, that is, the smallest system of subrings of $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ containing $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$ and the tautological subrings, which is also closed under pullbacks along forgetful maps and pushforwards along gluing maps. Recently, it has been shown that $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{11}_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ and $H^{13}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{13}_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for all $g$ and $n$. Meanwhile, $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}) \neq S_ω^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n})$ for all $n \geq 15$. Nevertheless, we prove that $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}) = S^{15}_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for all $n$. Moreover, we determine all relations in $S_ω^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for all $g \geq 2$ and give explicit bases for this vector space in terms of decorated graphs. Conditional upon the conjectured dimension of $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,14})$, we also prove that $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,n}) = S^{15}_ω(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,n})$ for all $n$. As an application, we prove $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = RH^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for several new small pairs $(g,n)$.

papers.title: The inf spectrum of moduli space
papers.abstract: Given a surface of genus $g \geq 2$, its inf spectrum is the ordered multiset of inf lengths of curves on the surface, the infimum being over all hyperbolic metrics. We show that the inf spectrum has exponential growth with coefficients that only depend on g, improving the earlier double exponential upper bound. The proof involves developing a number of tools including the process of "thickening" a surface and the notion of model surfaces. These tools may be of independent interest.

papers.title: The moduli space of cubic surfaces and its orbifold fundamental group
papers.abstract: We find a new presentation of the orbifold fundamental group of the moduli space of cubic surfaces, based on the Artin group of the Petersen graph. This group has two well-known quotients, which appear in the simplest possible way: killing the squares resp. sixth powers of our generators yields the Coxeter group $W(E_6)$ resp. a certain arithmetic group in $\operatorname{PU}(1,4)$. Along the way we present a certain central extension by $\mathbb{Z}$, of the genus zero mapping class group with any number of punctures. The $6$-puncture case is essential in this paper, and the general case may have independent interest.

papers.title: The modulo distinction problem for D*
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero and residue characteristic $p$. Let $E$ be a quadratic field extension of $F$. Let $D$ be the unique quaternion division algebra defined over $F$. Let $G=\GL_{2}(E)$ and $H=D^\times$. This paper studies the modulo distinction problem for the pair $(G,H)$ with $\ell\neq p$, which gives a complete classification of $H$-distinguished representations of $G$, including the cases $\ell=2$ and $p=2$. In terms of type theory, we give a complete classification of $H$-distinguished supercuspidal representations when $p$ is odd.

papers.title: The Quantum Character Transform
papers.abstract: Bastidas et al. (2025) highlighted the importance of exploiting group symmetries to reduce computational overhead and unify simulation methods across both condensed matter physics and ab initio quantum chemistry. I discuss the discrete character transform, which is the group Fourier transform restricted to $Z(\mathbb{C}[G])$, the center of the group algebra, where class functions form a commutative convolution algebra and irreducible characters are its spectral basis. The normalized character table of a non-abelian group can be obtained through a restriction operator, which means an efficient quantum character transform for any finite group with an efficient quantum Fourier transform. I give complementary quantum algorithms for class convolution based on direct class-sum block encoding and spectral implementation in the character basis, explaining their applications to symmetry-adapted many-body dynamics, molecular and spectroscopic symmetry analysis, and quantum walks, as well as characterizing the central information used in hidden-subgroup problems, including its limitations for graph isomorphism.

papers.title: The truncated octahedral conjecture
papers.abstract: Among three-dimensional parallelohedra of fixed volume, the Archimedean truncated octahedron uniquely minimizes surface area, affirming a conjecture of K. Bezdek from 2006. One inequality in the proof is verified by an exact computer-assisted certificate. The simplex, frame, and graphical-zonotope inequalities used in the proof hold in arbitrary dimension.

papers.title: Topological Classification of Univariate Sparse Polynomials via Tropical Geometry
papers.abstract: We give the topological classification of some simplest univariate complex fewnomials, and find tropical fans of the fewnomial strata with each topological type. Specifically, for the support $ A=\{d,d+1,d+2,d+3,d+4\},\quad d\geq3, $ we classify the topological equivalence classes of polynomials having two critical values of ramification type $(2,2)$. There is one class for odd $d$ and two classes for even $d$. We describe the branches at infinity of the corresponding one-dimensional stratum using Newton polytopes of certain complete intersection representations of the sought strata, and determine their tropicalizations. The combinatorial types of the obtained tropical polynomials distinguishes all three kinds of topological equivalence classes. These computations suggest a correspondence between topological equivalence classes of polynomials and combinatorial types of tropicalizations of their branches at infinity, as well as a possible periodicity phenomenon under translations of the support.

papers.title: Total Cohomology of Hilbert schemes of Orbisurfaces I: Reduction to Stacky Loci
papers.abstract: We generalize Nakajima's theory of Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces to Hilbert schemes of points on \textit{orbisurfaces}, and obtain initial factorization based on stratification by stabilizers. While the usual formula is retained for the trivial stabilizer stratum and for those strata of codimension $1$, genuine difficulties arise with stacky points strata. In the local picture of an isolated stacky point, the theory reduce to the study of $\Quot^\bfv[\CC^2/G]$ for a \textit{small} finite subgroup of $GL_2(\CC)$. The generating series for their total cohomology is a geometric correction of the generating series for total cohomology of ordinary smooth surface schemes. In addition, we obtain an action of the Borel-Moore homology of the punctual fibre stacks on the total Hilbert cohomology by virtual correspondences, in analogy with the Fock space description in Nakajima's theory. The punctual fibre stacks are genuinely different from the symmetric stack, and has natural realizations via motivic integration.

papers.title: Track objects in cubical presheaf automata
papers.abstract: Using the formalism of presheaf automata, we introduce new classes of automata for modelling concurrency that extend higher-dimensional automata and symmetric higher-dimensional automata. We study their languages and characterise these languages in terms of posetal cospans.

papers.title: Two indecomposable Enriques categories
papers.abstract: This note proves that the Kuznetsov component of a quartic double solid or a special Gushel-Mukai threefold does not have non-trivial admissible subcategories.

papers.title: Unipotent quotients in compactified Coxeter varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend Lusztig's description of quotients of Coxeter varieties by unipotent radicals of parabolic subgroups, to quotients of certain open neighbourhoods in the smooth compactification of Coxeter varieties. These quotients are products of an affine space with a Coxeter variety for an associated Levi quotient, and this result holds uniformly for any connected reductive group over a finite field. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Wang computing the invariants, under the action of unipotent subgroups, of the cohomology of the Deligne-Lusztig coverings of Coxeter varieties. We also prove that derived Alvis-Curtis duality sends the compactly supported cohomology of these coverings to their ordinary cohomology.

papers.title: Universal Varieties for Signatures of Membranes
papers.abstract: Membranes are sufficiently smooth vector-valued functions defined on the unit square, widely used in applications such as interpolation of image data. The signature of a membrane is a collection of nonlinear features that capture its essential geometry. We index these features in the graded Hopf algebra of two-parameter shuffle products and study the algebraic varieties for each graded component. At each truncation level, we obtain the dimension of this variety via a novel Witt-type formula. We propose a Chen-Chow theorem for membranes, provably at the second truncation level, and conjecturally for higher levels with extensive computational evidence in the computer algebra system OSCAR.

papers.title: Universality of $\mathsf{CohFT}$ of $\mathsf{Hilb}_n(S)$
papers.abstract: By virtue of their relation to Fulton--MacPherson compactifications, the cohomological field theory of Hilbert schemes of points on a surface, in extremal curve classes, is universally and effectively determined by the characteristic numbers of the surface and by the corresponding theory of Hilbert schemes of the affine plane. As a consequence, we compute the extremal genus 1 Gromov--Witten invariants of Hilbert schemes of all surfaces.

papers.title: Yangian for $\mathfrak{gl}_{2}$ and Gelfand-Tsetlin basis for $\mathfrak{gl}_{n}$
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit realization of finite-dimensional irreducible representations $V_λ$ of $\mathfrak{gl}_{n}$ using the representation theory of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})$. We consider $V_λ$ as the evaluation representation of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n})$ and restrict it to the subalgebras $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})^{(i)}$. Then $V_λ$ is completely reducible as a representation of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})^{(i)}$. It allows us to use the explicit formulas for irreducible representations of $\mathrm{Y}(\mathfrak{gl}_{2})$.
